lesson.menu_title: The Year Ahead — Forecasts and Roadmaps
lesson.menu_desc: Reading an annual roadmap and talking about the year ahead with four futures -- 30 slides
lesson.subtitle: Lesson 14 -- The Year Ahead: Forecasts and Roadmaps
lesson.title_tag: Professor View -- Marcio Ferreira Santos | Lesson 14 -- The Year Ahead

listenings.text: Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining. Let me start with the outlook, and then I am going to take your questions. Next year will not be easy. Food inflation will stay high in the first half, and that is our main headwind. But we are not waiting for it to pass. From January, we are going to review prices every quarter, and we are going to protect the basic basket: the pass-through on those items will be two percent at most. Some of you asked about the new stores. We are opening eight in the first half, and the contracts are already signed. On guidance, nothing changes today. At the current run rate, we will have reached our volume target by October. If that changes, you will hear it from me first, not from the market.

One question comes up in almost every visa interview, and most people answer it badly. What are your plans after the course? The officer is not asking about your dreams. The officer is checking that you are going home. So answer with three futures. First, the arrangement that is already fixed: I am flying back the day after the course ends. Second, the plan: I am going to use the pricing models with my team at work. Third, a date, and what will be finished by then: by the end of the year, I will have presented the results to my board. Short, concrete, and nothing about staying. And one practical detail. Bring the return ticket. A date on paper says more than any promise.

extra_audio.text: First, she gives the outlook in one sentence. Then she names the main headwind. After that, she says what is already decided. Next, she gives the dates that are already fixed. Finally, she says what will be finished by a certain date.

reading.rtitle: Commercial Pricing — Roadmap for Next Year
paras: This memo sets out the pricing roadmap for next year. The short version: our outlook is cautious, but the plan is clear. Food inflation will stay high in the first half, and it will be our main headwind. Freight and energy costs should fall after June, and that will be a tailwind in the second half.

Three decisions are already made. First, we are going to review prices every quarter, not every six months. Second, we are going to limit the pass-through on basic items to two percent, even if supplier costs rise faster. Third, we are not going to match every competitor promotion. We will match only on the fifty items that customers compare most.

Two dates are fixed. The board is meeting on February 12 to approve the plan, and the regional directors are presenting their targets on March 3. The new pricing tool is on track: by the end of March, we will have finished the rollout in all regions.

On the numbers, we are keeping our margin guidance. At the current run rate, we will reach the volume target in October, not in December. One warning, though: a forecast is not a promise. If the headwind is stronger than expected, we will review the guidance in the second quarter, and we will say so early.

gist.prompt: Read once for the main idea. What is the main message of the memo?
choices: Costs are going down everywhere next year, so the company can finally cut the price of every item on the shelf
The outlook is cautious, but the plan and the dates are already clear
The company is changing its margin guidance

The board meeting already has a date.
